trajectory_summary: The call opens with unusually high customer warmth and cooperation, and the rep moves efficiently through the verify checklist, landing a specific day-and-time appointment. But the rep never builds on the two strongest threads the customer handed him — the pool/gas cost pain and the estimated bill — and the military-spouse-benefit question was left open rather than resolved before booking. The call is efficient and outcome-positive but energy-flat: nothing the rep said deepened the customer's already-present interest.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Tuesday the 2nd) and time (2:30) are agreed upon and confirmed by the customer's thanks at 04:13, with the rep restating the hour block and date at 04:20-04:26. Co-owner confirmation is not applicable since the customer stated sole ownership at 01:56 with no other title holder to include.

Cool.' before moving to the next verify item — no attempt is made to turn the number, or the connected pool/gas cost pain from 00:37, into the customer's reason to act. The flip should have landed right here or at booking.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep never raises collecting the actual utility bill (mail, online, text, photo, email) at any point in the call; he relies solely on the customer's verbal estimate and moves straight to scheduling.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: So, yes, mainly for the pool.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asks the interest question and reflects the customer's answer back verbally at 01:10, which counts as capture, but he never references the pool/gas-cost motivation again — not at the bill discussion, not at booking, not in the close — so the reason was captured but not carried forward or used as leverage.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I asked the police. I'm gonna say it's gonna be, like, around, you know, $2.02 2 to $2.50.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer handed the rep two connected pain points — a gas-heated pool she called 'too crazy' expensive, and an estimated bill — within the first 90 seconds. The rep captured both but never reflected them back as the reason to act, at booking or in the close. This is the single highest-leverage miss on an otherwise cooperative, easy call.

key_moments.stewart_read: A pool heated by gas is a concrete, high-load use case the customer connects directly to cost pain — this is exactly the kind of anchor the schema wants surfaced and carried forward into the appointment framing.

The reflection is present; the leverage from it is not.
